text:
I see only the man who set himself ablaze in Concepción, who made smoke
of his flesh and burned for all Chile on the steps
of the cathedral before the troops without
blinking, without weeping, lit up and
exploded by a firedamp not of this World: I see
only the man who burned.

I see only Acevedo flaming there
for us, with a man's resolve, stern
and righteous, pine and
adobe, lighting the flight
of the disappeared along the whole
howling coast: I see only the man who burned.

I see only the white flag of his shirt
burn until the four corners of the square
turn red; I see only the lindens
weeping rough nitrogen
for his soul, crying out to heaven
for the return of a toqui
who will lead us out of this: I see only the man who burned.

I see only the deep Bío-Bío, father of waters, keeping watch
over the dead man: healer
of our wounds from Arauco
to today, nearly motionless in
its hoarse sleep and
sacred as the rehue, bearing
the mutilations of the whirl
of sand and blood with bodies at
the bottom, foretelling
resurrection: I see only the man who burned.

I see only the stain of love that
no one can ever tear from the cement, whether they wash it
with turpentine or caustic
soda, scrub it
with steel points, sand it
with nails and bullets, paint over it, deny it
on every screen of
lies from north to south: I see only the man who burned.

translation.title: Sebastián Acevedo
